You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer tests-fixtures):
- file: tests/fixtures/Makefile:137
- category: duplication
- title: Four identical rt_linux_* glibc rules could collapse to one static pattern rule
- detail: rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf (137-138), rt_linux_file.elf (142-143), rt_linux_time.elf (146-147), and rt_linux_mmap.elf (150-151) have byte-identical recipes: `$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall $< -o $@` with the same single-.c prerequisite. A list variable (e.g. RT_LINUX_GLIBC_FIXTURES := rt_linux_glibc_hello rt_linux_file rt_linux_time rt_linux_mmap) plus one static pattern rule `$(RT_LINUX_GLIBC_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c` replaces all four, and the clean list (lines 249-250) can reuse the variable. rt_linux_matvec.elf (157-159) stays separate: it adds -I $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include and the $(VPLAT_RT) dep. The per-rule roadmap comments (U5/U6/U7) can move onto the list entries.
- claimed safety: make -n before/after emits the same compile command per target with the same prerequisites; no target names, flags, or deps change.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
2	#
3	# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
4	# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
5	# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
6	# to bypass the env var.
7	
8	TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
9	# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
10	# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
11	# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
12	rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
13	CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
14	CXX       = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-g++
15	LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
16	OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump
17	
18	# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
19	# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
20	# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
21	RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
22	LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
23	# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
24	HELPERS_DIR := runtime
25	
26	CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
27	LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static
28	
29	# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
30	RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
31	               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
32	               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
33	               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
34	
35	# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
36	# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
37	# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
38	BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
39	                  break_verify_diverge
40	
41	# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
42	# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
43	# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
44	# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
45	# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
46	# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
47	# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
48	# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
49	# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
50	# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
51	RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
52	                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
53	RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
54	                    rt_c_hvm_data
55	RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file vplat_gettimeofday \
56	                       vplat_window
57	# C++ vplat smoke fixture: static ctors/dtors + libstdc++ containers
58	# through the same two-flag link, with g++ instead of gcc.
59	RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_cpp
60	
61	RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
62	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
63	# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
64	RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
65	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.c $(RUNTIME_DIR)/htif_client.h \
66	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
67	                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
68	VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
69	VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
70	                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
71	                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
72	VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
73	# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
74	# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
75	# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
76	VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
77	
78	# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
79	# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
80	# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
81	# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
82	# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
83	TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
84	CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
85	LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
86	CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
87	VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
88	VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
89	VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
90	                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
91	                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
92	
93	.PHONY: all clean dump rv32
94	
95	# Linux-ABI app fixtures (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U3+): -nostdlib, no
96	# andesim runtime at all -- vlinux is what sets these up, not crt0.S. Link
97	# base 0x10000, the roadmap's "App image" base; -e _start since there is no
98	# crt0 to fall into it via link order.
99	LINUX_APP_CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
100	LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS := -nostdlib -static -Wl,-e,_start -Wl,-Ttext=0x10000
101	
102	# Real static-glibc app fixtures (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4+): the vendor
103	# Linux-ABI toolchain (separate from HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN's bare-metal newlib
104	# one), ordinary static link -- no -Ttext override, the toolchain's own
105	# default static-exec layout (non-PIE, link base ~0x50000) just works with
106	# vlinux's loader as-is. Deferred to use-time (recursive `=` + $(error)) so
107	# `make all` (which does not need LINUX_TOOLCHAIN) is unaffected.
108	linux_glibc_tc = $(if $(strip $(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)),$(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN),$(error LINUX_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
109	GLIBC_CC = $(linux_glibc_tc)/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc
110	
111	all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
112	     rt_linux_argv.elf \
113	     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
114	     hvm_readback.elf \
115	     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
116	     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
117	     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)
118	
119	# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
120	# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
121	# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.
122	
123	spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
124		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
125		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@
126	
127	handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
128		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
129		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@
130	
131	rt_linux_argv.elf: rt_linux_argv.c
132		$(CC) $(LINUX_APP_CFLAGS) $(LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS) $< -o $@
133	
134	# NOT part of `all` -- needs the optional LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (env-gated, like
135	# the rv32 fixtures need HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32). Build individually:
136	# make rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf
137	rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf: rt_linux_glibc_hello.c
138		$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall $< -o $@
139	
140	# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U5: File I/O syscall set. Same toolchain/link as
141	# rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf; NOT part of `all` for the same reason.
142	rt_linux_file.elf: rt_linux_file.c
143		$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall $< -o $@
144	
145	# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U6: Time syscalls. Same toolchain/link.
146	rt_linux_time.elf: rt_linux_time.c
147		$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall $< -o $@
148	
149	# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U7: File-backed private mmap. Same toolchain/link.
150	rt_linux_mmap.elf: rt_linux_mmap.c
151		$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall $< -o $@
152	
153	# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U9: marker'd glibc kernel under hybrid. Same
154	# toolchain/link, plus the installed andesim/ROI.h include path (the same
155	# runtime/ build every vplat fixture uses via -B/-specs -- this fixture
156	# just needs the ONE header, not the whole bare-metal runtime).
157	rt_linux_matvec.elf: rt_linux_matvec.c $(VPLAT_RT)
158		$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall \
159		  -I $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include $< -o $@
160	
161	# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
162	# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
163	# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
164	# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
165	l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
166		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
167		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
168	lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
169	
170	# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
171	# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
172	# the exit code).
173	lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
174	                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
175		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
176	
177	# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
178	# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
179	hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
180		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
181	
182	$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
183		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
184		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
185	
186	# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
187	# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
188	$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
189		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
190		$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
191	
192	# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
193	# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
194	$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
195		$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
196		  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
197	
198	# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
199	# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
200	$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
201		$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
202		  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
203	rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

212	$(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.cpp $(VPLAT_RT)

216	$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)

240	$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
